markingScheme.criterion: Quotes at least one website name from the student's own Lookup rows together with the IP number DNS returned for it.
markingScheme.accept: Any pair that matches a Lookup row in the student's own record (e.g. www.zoo.org and 93.184.1.5).
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying 'DNS gives a number' with no name and number quoted from the record.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains that DNS (the Internet's phone book) translates the name into an IP address, which computers need to connect.
markingScheme.accept: 'It changes the name into numbers', 'it looks up the address', 'computers talk with numbers', 'forward lookup'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'DNS makes it work' with no idea of translating a name into an IP number.

markingScheme.criterion: States whether their Predict choice was right (the correct idea is that a DNS server turns the name into an IP number) and says why.
markingScheme.accept: Either 'my prediction was right/wrong' with a reason that matches the DNS idea.
markingScheme.insufficient: Repeating the prediction without judging it against the lookups.

markingScheme.criterion: Says the bank's web address should start with https:// (the padlock), not http://.
Explains why: https scrambles (encrypts) the data so someone watching the Wi-Fi cannot read the password, while plain http can be read.
markingScheme.accept: 'Hackers or snoopers cannot read it', 'it is secret/locked/encrypted', 'TLS or SSL protects it'.
markingScheme.insufficient: 'It is safer' with no idea that the data is scrambled or hidden from snoopers.

markingScheme.criterion: Names SMTP as the protocol that sends the email.
markingScheme.insufficient: IMAP or POP (those receive mail), or FTP/HTTP.
